paragraphs: יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיִשְׁתַּבַּח וְיִתְפָּאַר וְיִתְרוֹמַם וְיִתְנַשֵּׂא שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁהוּא רִאשׁוֹן וְהוּא אַחֲרוֹן וּמִבַּלְעָדָיו אֵין אֱלֹהִים סֹלּוּ לָרֹכֵב בָּעֲרָבוֹת בְּיָהּ שְׁמוֹ וְעִלְזוּ לְפָנָיו. וּשְׁמוֹ מְרוֹמָם עַל־כָּל־בְּרָכָה וּתְהִלָּה:
בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד:

Blessed and praised, glorified, exalted and extolled be the Name of the Supreme King of Kings, the Holy One blessed be He. He is the first and He is the last and beside Him there is no God. Make way before Him, who is enthroned above the clouds, Yah is his Name and rejoice before Him. His Name is exalted above all blessing and fame. Blessed be His glorious royal Name for ever and ever.
בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד:
Blessed be His glorious royal Name for ever and ever.

decisions: Yitbarakh ends before Yehi Shem; the latter Psalm113:2 has no English. Preserve the Hebrew two paragraphs against the English one paragraph under the same whole identity.
El Melekh Neeman has no English and is gated only at service occurrence for no minyan; יחיד אומר stays a rubric.
The quiet-recitation rubric belongs to the Barukh Shem service occurrence, not its reusable words.
Barekhu and Shema occurrences of the similar Barukh Shem sentence retain their established distinct canonical context identities.
